pending_findings.summary: The PR's service_order mechanism (call() next-entry selection, listOperational() display order, reorder() eligible cohort) completely bypasses the pre-existing priority_order contract specified in ARCHITECTURE.md:96-108 for exactly this feature ('optional persisted authorized override'; authoritative order is priority_order-cohort first, then eligibility_order; contiguous 1..N renumbering on cohort exit; 1..N+1 insert / 1..N move). priority_order is read everywhere in this diff's queue/index.ts but never written to a non-null value anywhere, and none of the three ordering-critical ORDER BY clauses include it. check_in also unconditionally assigns service_order to every checked-in entry, not just an authorized override, a materially different model than the spec. Originally flagged as P1 by Codex's own automated review bot on the very first commit (c6aa1b2604); missed by Claude across three review rounds focused on the separate CLAUDE-031/032 concurrency findings.
pending_findings.evidence: https://github.com/NTinkicht/Tabibi/pull/39#issuecomment-5561291800 (Claude's independent concurrence) and the original finding at https://github.com/NTinkicht/Tabibi/pull/39#issuecomment (second Claude pathway, same PR) -- both verified directly against ARCHITECTURE.md and a grep of priority_order usage in queue/index.ts at this exact head.
pending_findings.required_resolution: Either (a) implement ordering via priority_order per the existing ARCHITECTURE.md contract -- active cohort = waiting/checked_in with non-null priority_order, contiguous renumbering on cohort exit, 1..N+1 insert / 1..N move -- and make call()/listOperational() honor it ahead of eligibility_order/service_order; or (b) make an explicit architecture decision that service_order supersedes priority_order for this feature, documented in ARCHITECTURE.md, resolving the dual-field ambiguity (e.g. deprecate/remove priority_order).
pending_findings.verification_method: Architecture-doc/code cross-reference (as above); once resolved, a test asserting a non-null priority_order entry is called ahead of a lower-service_order non-priority entry, per the spec's stated precedence.

resolved_findings.resolution: Added reason: 'Patient left before being called' to the no_show command() call in the gap-regression test. Independently verified: diffed the two heads to confirm this was the only application/test change, then ran the full integration suite 3 consecutive times against real Postgres from a clean worktree (34/34 every run, all five files), plus typecheck/lint/format and unit+API. GitHub CI (run 34051506983) independently confirmed tied to this exact head, all green.

reorder() now bulk-sets service_order=NULL for the whole locked checked-in cohort (UPDATE ... WHERE id=ANY($1::uuid[])) before assigning final contiguous 1..length values, structurally removing every touched row from the partial unique index before any new value is written -- eliminating the gap-collision case entirely rather than relying on a safe offset. Also wraps the update in a try/catch translating 23505 to QueueConflictError as defense in depth. Independently re-verified: re-ran the original real-Postgres repro (check in 3, no_show the middle one, check in a 4th, reorder the first entry to the back) against this exact head in a fresh worktree -- it now succeeds with deterministic service_order [1,2,3], where it previously threw a raw 23505. Full existing suite (lifecycle/clinic-scheduling/walk-in/database/unit/API, typecheck, lint) also re-run clean. Note: GitHub CI had not actually run for this exact head at review time (author-confirmed empty check rollup); this resolution rests on independent local verification, not a CI badge.
